text:
olivia: Quick sync — infra hit yesterday means we need to lock cuts for launch next Wed. I propose a rollforward plan: ship core chat + embeddings, defer tenant routing and admin analytics to v1. Thoughts?

aakash: Can we flip that? Cut admin analytics but keep tenant routing. Tenant routing depends on the auth change but that's low-risk if we gate.

mike: Infra note: keeping tenant routing adds ~12ms p95 and requires an extra GPU slot during peak. Ops cost +1 dedicated node. tagging @taylor for tradeoff.

jess: Two-paths sound sensible: 1) "fast roll" = defer tenant routing + analytics; 2) "soft roll" = keep tenant routing behind a feature-flag per-tenant. Which path do we want? :thinking_face:

olivia: I'm leaning fast roll to minimize launch risk. We can provide a migration plan for customers and prioritize tenant routing in the first v1 sprint. Need decision today to freeze release.

taylor: I agree with fast roll. Add guardrails: if canary latency p95 > 200ms we hold and rollback. Sales can request exception for up to 2 enterprise tenants with explicit sign-off.

aakash: Ok — if we go fast roll I'll ship a small shim to emulate tenant headers for QA so integration work continues (ETA EOD).

jess: I'll update the launch checklist, release notes, and customer comms. Draft blurb: "Admin analytics removed from initial release to prioritize latency and reliability; returning in v1."

release-bot: deploy scheduled: branch release/2026-05-12 -> staging at 2026-05-10 14:00 UTC :shipit:

olivia: Action items: a) @aakash implement shim (ETA EOD) b) @mike confirm GPU allocation by 17:00 c) @jess update comms + release notes. I'll lock scope if all green.

mike: Confirmed — allocated extra slot, will monitor canary and alert on p95 drift.

aakash: Shim PR opened: `github.com/redwood/release/pull/412` — tests passing, leaving notes in PR for QA.

olivia: Thanks — locking scope to core chat + embeddings, deferring tenant routing/admin analytics to v1. Will post final scope update to handbook.
